correctness.rationale: Exact reducing-subspace diagonalization yields all preconditioned eigenvalues; positive α=s^-1 converts Type I to a ratio of extreme affine spectral bands. A full two-case monotonicity argument establishes the infima, all optimizing intervals, and strict improvement criterion; Type II is solved by placing unit between two scalar spectral extremes. Explicit 2×2 family attains arbitrary separation. The packaged standalone verification program passed 153030 finite numerical comparisons, which are not a substitute for the analytical proof.

value.rationale: The two concrete regularizations were recently proposed to make a singular RB inverse usable; it is a motivated tuning question whether they actually improve conditioning. The theorem gives complete sharp scalar choices and a striking strict-improvement phase boundary for Type I, plus a realizable unbounded gap to the projected-complement version. This is a natural invariant-subspace benchmark, not merely a numerical recomputation or arbitrary small instance.
